'''''Trachycarpus martianus''''' (also known as '''Martius' fan palm''') is a tree in the family [[Arecaceae]]. There are two distinct populations: one at {{convert|1500|m|ft|-3|abbr=on}} in the [[Khasia Hills]] of [[Meghalaya]] state, in northeast [[India]], the other at {{convert|2400|m|ft|-3|abbr=on}} in central northern [[Nepal]]. Other populations have been reported in [[Assam]], [[Sikkim]], [[Burma]] and southern [[China]].<ref name="kathetighe">[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=207163 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families, ''Trachycarpus martianus'']</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author = B. S. Kholia |title = Rediscovery of ''Trachycarpus martianus'' in the Sikkim Himalaya |url = http://www.palms.org/palmsjournal/2012/vol56n1p5-10.pdf |journal = Palms |date=March 2012 |volume = 56 |issue = 1}}</ref> The main identifying characteristics are the regular leaf splits (to about halfway), the coffee-bean-shaped seeds (similar looking to ''[[Trachycarpus latisectus]]'') and the bare, as opposed to fibrous trunk. The new leaf spear and edges of the petioles are covered with a white tomentum.<ref>Martin Gibbons. ''A pocket guide to Palms''.</ref><ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/250679#page/435/mode/1up Wendland, Hermann A. 1861.  Bulletin de la Société Botanique de France 8: 429, ''Trachycarpus martianus''].</ref><ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/452197#page/23/mode/1up Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1831.  Plantae Asiaticae Rariores 3: 5–6, t. 211, ''Chamaerops martiana'' ]</ref>

The species is named after the German botanist [[Carl Friedrich Philipp von Martius]] (1794-1868).<ref name=Genaust1983>Genaust, Helmut (1976). ''Etymologisches Wörterbuch der botanischen Pflanzennamen'' {{ISBN|3-7643-0755-2}}</ref>

It is used in making Jhapi, a traditional head cover often used to felicitate guests in Assam.
